en.title: Draw the Letter Y by Changing the Fewest Cells
en.description:
You are given a square matrix of odd order whose cell values are only 0, 1, or 2. Choose one digit as the digit of the Y: its upper part consists of the two diagonals running from the top-left corner to the center and from the top-right corner to the center, and below the center it is the middle column; every cell outside the Y must become one other, different digit. Find the minimum number of cells that must be changed.

Standard input/output, this site's supplementary ranges, and the examples follow this problem's description.
en.input: The first line contains an odd n (1≤n≤99), followed by n lines, each with n values of 0, 1, or 2. The upper bound on n is a site supplement.
en.output: Output the minimum number of cells to change.
en.explanation: Determine for each cell whether it belongs to the Y, and count the 0s, 1s, and 2s inside and outside the Y separately. Enumerate the six distinct (Y digit, background digit) pairs, compute the number of mismatched cells, and take the minimum.
